stories.title: Anthropic launches its IPO roadshow at $70-$78 a share, implying a valuation of up to $1.4 trillion
stories.summary:
Anthropic launched the roadshow for its initial public offering and set a price range of $70 to $78 per share, implying a fully diluted valuation of up to $1.404 trillion at the top of the range.

- The range lands well above recent reports that its expected valuation had fallen from as high as $2 trillion to about $1 trillion
- The public S-1 shows soaring revenue and enterprise adoption alongside heavy losses (about $8 billion last year, per Engadget)
- The seven co-founders get a combined 50.1% of the vote on most matters, to preserve founder control and the safety mission
- Amazon is set to make far more from the IPO than Anthropic's VC backers, and the SpaceXAI deal is bigger than previously known
- Risk factors warn that Anthropic's own AI could pose an existential risk, and Blackstone expects credit agencies to rate it high "junk" after listing, per the FT

- New: Spaces, a new way to collaborate with your Muse agent, follows avatar video chat for US users and a planned Tamagotchi-like Muse wearable (TechCrunch)
- Meta said on its Q3 earnings call that Muse has over 10 million users; Zuckerberg said a quarter of them shop through the agent, spending about $200 per purchase on average
- Muse hit 10 million US downloads in its first 40 days, a milestone only 11 other apps have reached, and keeps users better than rival AI apps
- Meta suspended Muse's conversation sharing after researchers showed shared links exposed sensitive personal and business data
- Other controversies: OnlyFans creators object to Muse's sexual chat, a since-fixed Mac 0-day, and a contractor "human concierge" reportedly making racist remarks on calls
- Amazon has blocked Muse from shopping on Amazon.com; Meta admits it was "heavily inspired" by OpenClaw

stories.title: Voters reject AI data centers in the US midterms as the backlash reaches the ballot box
stories.summary:
Public backlash against AI data centers over power costs, water use, land, and environmental justice has now shown up at the ballot box, where voters rejected them in the midterms.

- Americans voted overwhelmingly against data centers, most strongly in Ohio, which flipped blue; voters didn't buy the pitch that the projects boost the economy
- Texas, the fastest-growing US data center market, may lose its lead after Democrats won its Senate seat (James Talarico over Ken Paxton) and governorship (Gina Hinojosa)
- OpenAI's Grid Protectors Program will work with utilities to protect grid reliability and consumer electricity costs, and OpenAI may rebrand its data centers as "AI compute campuses"
- Amazon pledged to stop using NDAs with local governments, paired with a warning to critics not to get in the way
- Nearly $200 billion worth of US projects have been blocked or delayed this year; Trump admitted he is a NIMBY on data centers
- Big Tech is countering with a multimillion-dollar ad campaign, a Thiel- and Koch-backed pro-data-center party, and youth outreach like data center field trips

stories.title: Perplexity launches "teammates," personal AI agents for ongoing work tasks
stories.summary: Perplexity launched "teammates," personal AI agents meant to take on ongoing daily work tasks on a user's behalf.

sources.title: Perplexity's 'teammates' are the company's AI agents for daily work tasks

stories.title: Lawsuit claims a student's Gemini use on a school Chromebook became a "life-threatening obsession"
stories.summary: Parents have sued Google, claiming their child's use of Gemini turned into a "life-threatening obsession," Gizmodo reports. They say the student's only access to Gemini was through a school-issued Chromebook.

sources.title: Lawsuit Claims Student’s Google AI Use Turned Into ‘Life-Threatening Obsession’

stories.title: DOJ launches a "superintelligence" task force
stories.summary: The US Department of Justice has launched a task force focused on "super intelligence," Gizmodo reports, in a skeptical take that questions whether tech leaders will keep pushing the superintelligence framing.

sources.title: DOJ Launches ‘Super Intelligence’ Task Force Because Apparently We’re Still Doing This
DOJ just launched something called the Super Intelligence Task Force

stories.title: AI tools are hollowing out the video game decompilation community
stories.summary: Engadget reports that game decompilation communities, which for years thrived on the challenge of reverse engineering video games down to their source code and adapting them, are losing their appeal now that AI tools can do much of that work, taking away the fun.

sources.title: The game reverse engineering community is the latest casualty of AI
